gap_records.summary: Required candidate file for `tauri_source_manifest` is unverified.

acceptance_requirements: All acceptance evidence is candidate-bound and produced by the registered runtime replay and evidence exporter, never by static substitutes.
The auth segment of the PRD section 3 first-run path completes with durable data and recoverable failures.
Every reachable auth state shows intentional loading, empty or error, retry, unauthorized, and success treatment per PRD section 8.
Visual comparison checks hierarchy, whitespace, typography scale, icon usage, and absence of prohibited patterns against PRD 9.1.
Security review confirms hashed passwords, single-use expiring tokens, no secrets in logs or IPC, and uniform unknown-email handling.
Persistence review confirms user, session, and email-token records survive an application restart.
deferred_items: First-run path steps 5-11: project creation, task capture, Today and Calendar views, board movement, focus sessions, reminders, and cross-restart persistence review.
Forgot-password and reset flow with its email action pages; the auth shell reserves the entry point without implementing it this loop.
Settings surface: profile, timezone, notification preferences, password change, sessions list, and account deletion request.
Production email provider adapter with environment-configured secrets and delivery-state retry UI.
Inbox quick-add, search and filters; board drag-and-drop and its keyboard alternative; calendar month and agenda views.
Dark or alternate theming; not requested by the PRD and excluded from this loop.

extension_candidates.authority: PRD and Runtime remain authoritative; candidate is not a requirement until adopted

acceptance: Remembered email appears pre-filled only after explicit opt-in, clears via a visible control, and never restores a session.
candidate.cost: Small: one local preference, an opt-in control on the sign-in form, a visible clear control, and state coverage additions.
dependencies: completed auth slice with durable local storage
candidate.product_value: Faster repeat sign-in and fewer typographical errors in the entry action, deepening the PRD's promise of capturing the next useful action without friction.
candidate.rationale: Repeat sign-in on a personal desktop workspace is frequent, so an opt-in remembered email speeds the primary action; it is proposed now only because the auth shell is being built, and it stays deferred because loop budget is fully spent on the release-critical path and the shared-machine privacy tradeoff needs an explicit product decision.
candidate.risk: Persisting an email locally can conflict with shared-machine privacy expectations and slightly widens what local storage reveals; must be strictly opt-in and clearable.

extension_summary.authority: only active_ids may enter the current Developer objective

implied_completion: PRD section 3 steps 1-4 define this loop's slice; steps 5-11 (project, task, calendar, focus, reminder, and persistence review) are the remaining first-run path.
Offline development implies a local mail sink or provider sandbox for verification email; production provider adapters stay deferred.
Session persistence across refresh implies a webview-surviving mechanism such as a scoped cookie or equivalent, not in-memory state.
Server-side hashing and authorization imply the auth boundary lives in the Rust host behind IPC rather than in webview scripts.
The minimal durable schema for this slice is User, Session, and EmailToken; Project, Task, Subtask, Reminder, FocusSession, and ActivityEvent arrive with later increments.
Section 8 email action pages imply in-app handling for consumed and expired verification links with explicit recovery.
mandatory_objectives: The candidate runs as a native Tauri desktop app whose landing surface is the PRD auth shell.
Create account, verification via local mail sink, sign in, and sign out complete end to end with durable user, session, and email-token records.
Passwords exist only as server-side hashes; verification tokens are single-use and expiring; auth failures never reveal account existence.
Session state survives a webview reload and is cleared by explicit sign-out.
The auth surface follows PRD 9.1 visual direction and covers loading, error, retry, unauthorized, and success states with keyboard-visible focus.
task_specification.objective: Turn the bare Tauri bootstrap into the first reviewable vertical slice of Focusboard: a native desktop app whose landing surface is the PRD auth shell, with working account creation, single-use email verification through a local mail sink, sign in and sign out, and durable session persistence implemented on the Rust side of the IPC boundary. The slice must produce candidate-bound runtime, interface, persistence, security, and visual evidence sufficient for the prd_implementation_review phase gate and must follow the PRD section 9.1 visual direction. First-run path steps after authentication remain deferred to later loops.

diagnosis.root_cause: Not a defect but a phase-entry gap: the candidate is a bare Tauri bootstrap (src-tauri/Cargo.toml is a placeholder package without Tauri dependencies, src-tauri/tauri.conf.json still names 'HoH PRD Bootstrap', and no application source, UI, or storage code exists), so the frozen phase check prd_implementation_review has no runtime, interface, persistence, security, or visual product evidence to review. The selected increment must convert this skeleton into the first reviewable vertical slice of the PRD's release-critical first-run path.

stop_conditions: Stop and report blocked if the registered replay operation cannot launch the candidate after doctor diagnostics; never substitute static or external evidence.
Stop if any implementation path requires external network email delivery; the offline environment must use a local mail sink or sandbox.
Stop expanding into projects, tasks, inbox, calendar, focus, reminders, or Settings; those surfaces belong to later loops.
Stop and report if a required change falls outside the candidate directory or would touch frozen inputs or host-owned evidence.

strategy.rationale: The phase gate reviews runtime, interface, persistence, security, and visual evidence against the PRD, but the candidate holds only bootstrap placeholders with no product surface. The smallest coherent increment that can satisfy a qualitative review is the release-critical path's entry slice: auth shell through verified, durable sign-in, which exercises all five evidence dimensions at once. Work on tasks, projects, or reminders would depend on an authenticated workspace and could not produce reviewable evidence this loop.

code: Unit checks in the candidate cover password hashing round-trip, token expiry and single-use consumption, and session revocation.
Auth IPC commands reject unverified or revoked sessions and never echo password material or tokens.
runtime: Host replay shows create-account, local mail sink verification link, sign in, webview reload with session intact, and sign out in sequence.
Deliberate failure cases (wrong password, unverified account, reused or expired token) land in explicit recoverable states without fabricated success.
visual: Auth shell captures at wide and narrow widths show the PRD 9.1 hierarchy: primary sign-in action, calm editorial canvas, restrained accent, and no dark-blue full-page background.
Loading, error, and success states of the auth forms are captured with visible focus indication and readable field errors.

done_when: The candidate launches as a native desktop app whose landing surface is the auth shell, with create-account visually primary and no prohibited dark-blue full-page panel.
Creating an account with a valid email and password durably stores a user record whose password exists only as a hash, verifiable in the local datastore and logs.
Verification consumes a single-use expiring token delivered to the local mail sink; reuse and expired tokens are rejected with explicit recovery states.
Sign in with a verified account opens the signed-in workspace state; the session survives a webview reload and explicit sign-out clears it.
Unverified sign-in is blocked with an explicit state and a resend action, and wrong-password, unknown-email, and reused-token responses never reveal whether an unrelated email exists.
Auth forms expose loading, error, retry, and success states with field-associated validation and keyboard-visible focus.
Candidate-bound visual captures of the auth shell at wide and narrow widths match the PRD 9.1 hierarchy, spacing, and typography properties.
tasks.instructions: Deliver the auth vertical slice of the release-critical first-run path (PRD section 3 steps 1-4) as the first reviewable product increment. Make the native desktop window open the auth shell as the landing surface with a visually primary sign-in and create-account action per PRD 9.1. Implement registration, single-use expiring email verification through a local mail sink, sign in and sign out, and session persistence across webview reload. Store user, session, and email-token records durably on the Rust side of the IPC boundary: passwords only as server-side hashes, uniform unknown-email responses, minimal rate limiting or equivalent protection on auth commands, and no secrets in logs or IPC payloads. Cover loading, error, retry, unauthorized, and success states with field-associated validation messages and visible keyboard focus, and update the application identity away from the bootstrap placeholder. File layout beyond the listed targets stays the developer's choice; do not start projects, tasks, inbox, calendar, focus, reminders, Settings, or forgot/reset-password surfaces this loop. Self-validate in the candidate only; host replay and evidence recapture remain host-owned.

risk_note.summary: Runtime replay and visual capture on a first-boot Tauri skeleton is the validation most likely to end insufficient_evidence if the native window or webdriver bridge fails to launch.
risk_note.validation: Run the registered doctor/replay path (focusboard-native-webdriver) early and capture runtime_state plus auth-shell screenshots; if replay cannot launch, report blocked with the failure output instead of substituting static or external evidence.
risk_note.why_now: Loop 1 starts from a bare bootstrap (placeholder Cargo.toml without Tauri dependencies and a placeholder tauri.conf.json), so the runtime wiring is exercised for the first time and no prior replay evidence exists.
